name: Adventure Aquarium
facts: Formerly the Thomas H. Kean New Jersey State Aquarium.
Reopened in its current form on May 25, 2005.
Home to about 8,000 animals in freshwater, marine and semi-aquatic habitats.
Founded in 1992
Run by Herschend Family Entertainment
Address: 1 Riverside Drive, Camden

name: AMC Broadstreet 7
summary: Movie theater on North Broad Street, Philadelphia.
facts: Opened December 5, 2006 as the Pearl Theatre at Avenue North, next to Temple University.
Named for the former Pearl Theatre on Ridge Avenue and in memory of entertainer Pearl Bailey.
AMC took over management in September 2016.
Has seven screens.
Part of the AMC chain
Address: 1600 North Broad Street, Philadelphia

name: AMC Dine-In Fashion District 8
facts: Opened on November 4, 2019 on the third floor of the Fashion District mall.
Has eight screens and 870 seats, with its own entrance at 11th and Filbert Streets.
The mall was formerly known as the Gallery.
Part of the AMC chain
Also known as AMC Theaters at Fashion District Philadelphia

name: Annenberg Center for the Performing Arts
facts: Founded in 1971 and owned by the University of Pennsylvania.
The facility was designed by Vincent G. Kling, who also designed the Philadelphia Mint.
Includes the Zellerbach Theatre and the Harold Prince Theatre.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 3680 Walnut Street, Philadelphia

name: Arden Theatre
facts: Arden Theatre Company was formed in 1988.
Main property has the 175-seat Arcadia Stage and the 360-seat F. Otto Haas Stage.
The 100-seat Bob and Selma Horan Studio Theater is at 62 N 2nd Street in the Hamilton Family Arts Center.
Run by Arden Theatre Company
Address: 40 North 2nd Street, Philadelphia

name: Bushfire Theatre of Performing Arts
facts: Founded in 1977 by Alfred Simpkins as an African-American professional theatre company.
Housed in the old Locust Street Theater, a former vaudeville house turned movie house.
The 428-seat space on 52nd Street is home to its resident ensemble.
Established a Walk of Fame honoring African Americans of stage, screen and television in 1996.

name: Cinemark University City Penn 6
summary: Movie theatre. Does not allow bags or backpacks.
facts: Has six screens and 1,179 seats.
Cinemark took over the theater in June 2013.
Part of the Cinemark chain
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 4012 Walnut Street, Philadelphia

name: City Winery
facts: Address: 990 Filbert Street

name: ComedySportz
facts: Performs at The Adrienne Theater in the Rittenhouse section of Center City.
Flagship show is ComedySportz, a competitive improv comedy match.
Address: 2030 Sansom Street, Philadelphia

name: F. M. Kirby Auditorium
facts: Located inside the National Constitution Center at 525 Arch Street.
Has a permanent stage and a capacity of 209 guests.
Run by National Constitution Center

name: Forrest Theatre
facts: Named for the 19th century actor Edwin Forrest, who was born in Philadelphia.
Opened with a performance of The Red Robe.
Opened in 1928
Designed by Herbert J. Krapp
Owned by The Shubert Organization
Opened in 1927
Run by The Shubert Organization
Address: 1114 Walnut Street, Philadelphia

name: Franklin Music Hall
facts: Formerly the Electric Factory, renamed in October 2018 after a public naming contest.
Housed in a former General Electric Switchgear Plant building from 1916.
Sold to The Bowery Presents in September 2018.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 421 North 7th Street, Philadelphia

name: Freedom Mortgage Pavilion
facts: Outdoor amphitheater and indoor theater complex on the Camden Waterfront, across the Delaware River from Philadelphia.
Formerly the Blockbuster-Sony Music Entertainment Centre, Tweeter Center, Susquehanna Bank Center and BB&T Pavilion.
Renamed Freedom Mortgage Pavilion in May 2022.
Founded in 1995
Run by Live Nation Entertainment

name: Freedom Theatre
facts: African-American theatre company founded in 1966 by John E. Allen Jr.
Moved in 1968 into the Edwin Forrest House on North Broad Street.
Pennsylvania's oldest African-American theatrical institution.
Includes a 299-seat proscenium theatre named for John E. Allen, Jr.
Also known as New Freedom Theatre

name: Fringe Arts
summary: Theater on North Christopher Columbus Boulevard, Philadelphia.
facts: Address: 140 North Christopher Columbus Boulevard, Philadelphia

name: Helium Comedy Club
facts: Hosts headline comedy shows and open mic nights.
Has two full-service bars and serves appetizers, sandwiches, entrees and desserts.
Address: 2031 Sansom Street, Philadelphia

name: Iron Gate Theater
facts: Built in 1886 and designed by architect Theophilus Parsons Chandler.
Located in a national historic landmark building that also houses the Tabernacle Church and the Christian Association.
The former church sanctuary was converted to a theater without altering the interior.
Run by University of Pennsylvania

name: Irvine Auditorium
facts: Opened in May 1929 and built between 1926 and 1932.
Houses the Curtis Organ, nearly 11,000 pipes, built for the 1926 Sesquicentennial Exposition and donated in 1928.
Restored and renovated in 1997 to 2000 by Venturi, Scott Brown & Associates.
Designed by Horace Trumbauer
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 3401 Spruce Street, Philadelphia

name: Kurtz Performing Arts Center
facts: Opened in January 2010 at William Penn Charter School.
A LEED Gold certified building with a green roof.
Named by the Kurtz family in memory of David L. Kurtz.
Also known as Kurtz Center

name: Lantern Theater Company
facts: Run by Lantern Theater Company
Also known as St. Stephen's Theater
Address: 923 Ludlow Street, Philadelphia

name: Louis Bluver Theatre
summary: Theater on South Hicks Street, Philadelphia.
facts: Address: 302 South Hicks Street, Philadelphia

name: MacGuffin Theatre & Film Co
facts: Runs an after-school program for students.
Runs an acting camp.
Address: 2030 Sansom Street, Philadelphia

name: Mandell Theatre
facts: A 424-seat proscenium theater.
Primary performance venue for the Theater, Music and Dance programs at Drexel University.
Stands at the corner of 33rd and Chestnut Streets, between the Creese Student Center and MacAlister Hall.
Run by Drexel University
Address: 3220 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia

name: Marian Anderson Hall
facts: Formerly Verizon Hall, renamed Marian Anderson Hall in June 2024.
Home of the Philadelphia Orchestra, named for contralto and civil rights activist Marian Anderson.
Run by Kimmel Center for the Performing Arts

name: MilkBoy Philadelphia
facts: Created by Tommy Joyner and Jamie Lokoff of MilkBoy Recording Studio.
Combines a restaurant, bar and cafe with an upstairs live music venue.
Has two full bars.
Address: 1100 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia

name: Miller Theater
summary: Theater on South Broad Street, Philadelphia.
facts: Originally the Sam S. Shubert Theatre, built by the Shubert brothers in 1918 to honor their late brother Sam.
Formerly the Merriam Theater, it was purchased by the Kimmel Center in November 2016.
Renamed for Alan B. Miller, a founding board member of the Kimmel Center.
Run by University of the Arts
Address: 250 South Broad Street, Philadelphia

name: Old Academy Players
facts: Formed in 1923 as the Moment Musical Club by 19 members of the Falls Methodist Church.
Has used the Old Academy building in East Falls since 1932.
Grace Kelly began her acting career on its stage in 1942.

name: Perelman Theater
facts: Run by Kimmel Center for the Performing Arts
Address: 300 South Broad Street

name: PFS Bourse Theater
summary: Movie theater on Ranstead Street, Philadelphia.
facts: Opened in 1990 as the Ritz at the Bourse.
Philadelphia Film Society took over operation in 2021 and renovated all five theaters.
Has 5 screens
Address: 400 Ranstead Street, Philadelphia

name: PFS East Theater
summary: Movie theater on South 2nd Street, Philadelphia.
facts: Opened in 1981 as the Budco Olde City 2 and became the Ritz East in 1999.
Philadelphia Film Society acquired the theater in 2022.
Has 2 screens
Part of the Philadelphia Film Society chain
Address: 125 South 2nd Street, Philadelphia

name: Philadelphia Shakespeare Theatre
facts: Founded in 1989 as the Red Heel Theatre.
Changed its name and purpose in 1993.
Address: 2111 Sansom Street, Philadelphia

name: Plays & Players Theatre
facts: Founded in 1911, one of the oldest professional theater companies in the United States.
Building designed in 1912 by architect Amos W. Barnes as a dramatic school.
Murals were added in 1923 by artist Edith Emerson.
Address: 1712 Delancey Place, Unit 16, Philadelphia

name: Prince Music Theatre
facts: Bought by the Philadelphia Film Society in March 2015 and renamed Prince Theater.
Now operated by the Film Society as the Film Society Center.
Opened in 1921
Address: 1412 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia

name: Punch Line Philly
summary: Theater on East Laurel Street, Philadelphia.
facts: Comedy club in Fishtown with about 300 seats, booked by Live Nation's House of Blues Entertainment division.
Has a lobby bar serving craft beers and pub grub, plus an outdoor patio.
Hosts local talent showcases and burlesque shows.
Address: 33 East Laurel Street, Philadelphia

name: Ralph J. Roberts Forum
facts: Two-floor, 500-person amphitheater inside the Comcast Technology Center.
Named for Comcast founder Ralph J. Roberts.
Hosts movie premieres, keynote speakers, talent panels and book signings.

name: Reel Cinemas
summary: Movie theater on North Narberth Avenue, Narberth.
facts: Address: 129 North Narberth Avenue, Narberth

name: Regal UA Main Street Theatre
summary: Movie theater on Main Street, Philadelphia.
facts: Part of the Regal Cinemas chain
Address: 3720 Main Street, Philadelphia

name: Ritz Five
summary: Movie theater on Walnut Street, Philadelphia.
facts: Founded by Ramon L. Posel as a three-screen theatre in 1976 and expanded to five screens in 1985.
Premiered M. Night Shyamalan's debut feature Praying with Anger in 1992.
Ownership transferred to Landmark Theatres in March 2007.
Has 5 screens
Address: 214 Walnut Street, Philadelphia

name: Sidequest Theatre
facts: Grew out of Roll Play, an improvised comedy show paying tribute to tabletop role-playing games.
Opened in the former Adrienne Theater space, which became vacant in June 2023.
Offers improv and role-playing classes plus a summer camp for ages 11 to 14.
Neighbors Helium Comedy Club and ComedySportz on Sansom Street.
Address: 2030 Sansom Street, Philadelphia

name: Sidney Kimmel Theater
facts: Hosts Freedom Rising, a 17-minute 360-degree multimedia show with a live narrator.
Reopened on June 14, 2016 after its renovation.
Run by National Constitution Center

name: Skyline Stage
facts: Smaller open-air stage on the Highmark Mann campus in West Fairmount Park.
Wheelchair accessible

name: Strawberry Mansion Music Pavilion
facts: Designed in 1905 by Horace Trumbauer.
Had about 3,000 bench seats and was replaced by Robin Hood Dell in 1930.
The brick arches across from the Dell Music Center are a 1930s restroom complex on its foundation.

name: Suzanne Roberts Theatre
summary: Theater on South Broad Street, Philadelphia.
facts: Seats 365 people.
Named for Suzanne Roberts, an actress, playwright and director who hosted the TV program Seeking Solutions.
Her husband, Ralph J. Roberts, founded Comcast.
Opened in 2007
Designed by KieranTimberlake
Named after Suzanne Fleisher Roberts
Also known as Philadelphia Theatre Company
Address: 480 South Broad Street, Philadelphia

name: Temple Performing Arts Center
facts: Built as the Baptist Temple for the congregation led by pastor Russell Conwell.
Sold to Temple University in 1974.
Renovated in 2010 into a multipurpose performance venue with about 1,200 seats.
Includes two spaces, Lew Klein Hall and the Chapel.
Founded in 1891
Designed by Thomas Preston Lonsdale
Address: 1837 North Broad Street

name: The Mann Center
facts: Opened in 1976 as Robin Hood Dell West, summer home of the Philadelphia Orchestra.
Renamed Mann Music Center in 1979 in honor of Fredric R. Mann.
Campus includes an amphitheater, TD Pavilion and the Skyline Stage.
Signed a naming rights deal with Highmark in 2025.
Also known as Mann Center for the Performing Arts
Address: 5201 Parkside Avenue, Philadelphia

name: The Met
facts: Built in 1908 by impresario Oscar Hammerstein I as the ninth opera house he built.
Reopened on December 3, 2018 after a 2017-18 renovation.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Has three spaces: the Met Lobby, the Grand Salle and the theater.
Run by Live Nation

name: The Rotunda
facts: Building dates to 1911 and was originally built as a house of worship.
The University of Pennsylvania acquired the building in 1996.
A 1998 Urban Studies seminar led to the Foundation Community Arts Initiative, which began producing events there.
Run by University of Pennsylvania
Address: 4014 Walnut Street, Philadelphia

name: The Tower Theater
facts: Built in 1927 and opened the next year by John H. McClatchy as one of Upper Darby's first movie houses.
Showed both vaudeville acts and movies in its early years.
Seating capacity is 3,119.

name: The Universal Sphere
facts: A 360-degree dome theater in the Comcast Technology Center lobby at 1800 Arch Street.
Created by Steven Spielberg, DreamWorks Animation, Universal Destinations & Experiences and Comcast Labs.
Named a Certified Autism Center.

name: Theatre Exile
facts: Won multiple awards at the 2015 Barrymore Awards.
Address: 1340 South 13th Street, Unit 48, Philadelphia

name: Theatre of Living Arts
facts: The building dates to the early 1900s as a nickelodeon.
Became a regional theater led by Andre Gregory in the 1960s, named Theatre of the Living Arts.
The Philadelphia Council for the Performing Arts acquired the derelict cinema in 1964.
Capacity is 800.
Opened in 1908
Owned by Live Nation Entertainment
Also known as TLA
Address: 334 South Street, Philadelphia

name: Venice Island Performing Arts and Recreational Facility
facts: Opened with a celebration of live music and art in October 2014.
The transformation received a 2015 Groundbreaker Award.
Address: 7 Lock Street, Philadelphia

name: Walnut Street Theatre
facts: Founded in 1808 and the oldest operating theatre in the United States.
Was the first theatre to install gas footlights, in 1837.
Hosted the first presidential debate between Gerald Ford and Jimmy Carter on September 23, 1976.
Has three stages: the Mainstage, Independence Studio on 3 and Studio 5.
Opened in 1809
Designed by William Strickland
Built in the Neoclassical architecture style
Address: 825 Walnut Street, Philadelphia

name: Walter K Gordon Theater
facts: A 650-seat proscenium theater with an unobstructed view from every seat.
The hub of the performing arts at Rutgers-Camden.
Run by Rutgers University–Camden

name: Wilma Theater
summary: Theater on South Broad Street, Philadelphia.
facts: Current 296-seat theater opened in 1996 and was designed by Hugh Hardy.
Began in 1973 as the Wilma Project, which produced original material.
Blanka and Jiri Zizka joined in 1979 as artists-in-residence and later renamed it the Wilma Theater.
Received the 2024 Regional Theatre Tony Award.
Address: 265 South Broad Street, Philadelphia
